To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the basement membrane is the main reservoir of paracrinically acting growth factors in the tooth germ.

(1) the basement membrane plays a role in the initiation of odotoblast differentiation and in the spatial control of its initiation; (2) TGFβ3 and FGF1 are involved in the initiation of differentiation and in the propagation of differentiation gradients; and (3) IGF1 is involved in the initiation and propagation of differentiation gradients, and in the regulation of functional differentiation.

(1) the BM is a major regulator of odontoblastic differentiation, (2) immobilization and presentation of TGFβs is a major mechanism by which this is accomplished, and (3) the initiation of odotoblastic differentiation may be controlled by the BM, whereas propagation is controlled by TGFβs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms that control odontoblast terminal and functional differentiation.
the molecular mechanisms controlling the initiation and propagation of odontobast differentiation.
the molecular mechanisms controlling odontoblast terminal cell differentiation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the differentiation of odontblast requires the interaction of the epithelium and the underlying BM, and the BM is a major reservoir of paracrinically acting growth factors.
the initiation and propagation of odontobast differentiation are controlled by a combination of epigenetic signals, including the spatial presentation of active TGFβs.
the initiation of odonto-blast differentiation is controlled by the dental papilla, and its maintenance is regulated by the inner enamel epithelium.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the initiation of odntoblast differentiation is controlled by the epithelium and the basement membrane and that its propagation is controlled by the basement membrane.
the differentiation of odontogenic mesenchyme into odontoblast-like cells is regulated in a spatio-temporal manner by the epithelium.
the initiation of odonto-blast differentiation is controlled by the BM and that its propagation requires the combined action of immobilized TGF(3) and heparan sulfate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the initiation and propagation of odontobast differentiation is regulated by a combination of cell autonomous and cell non-autonomous mechanisms.
differentiation of odontblast cells is controlled by the epithelium through a paracrine mechanism involving the basement membrane and that it is possible to reproduce this process in vitro.
odontoblastic differentiation is a complex process involving the interaction of several signaling molecules and the BM.
